question: What is a bone fracture?

options.A: A stretching injury to skeletal muscle fibers
options.B: A severe infection inside the bone marrow
options.C: A complete tearing of a ligament near a joint
options.D: A break or disruption in the continuity of a bone

explanation: Simple and clear! A fracture just means the bone's structure has cracked or broken. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h1)

question: Why is a home health nurse so important after a patient goes home with a broken bone?

options.A: To prescribe stronger narcotic pain medications when healing slows down
options.B: To monitor ongoing recovery and prevent long-term immobility complications
options.C: To perform immediate open reduction surgery inside the patient's home
options.D: To replace the hospital surgeon during routine follow-up visits

explanation: Most healing happens outside the hospital. Home nurses are vital for catching early warning signs and helping patients recover safely at home. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h1)

question: Which type of fracture happens when the broken bone pushes through the skin?
explanation: When bone breaks through the skin, it's called an open (or compound) fracture. This requires extra care because of the high risk of infection! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h2)

question: Why are greenstick fractures much more common in young children than in adults?

options.A: Children have much higher calcium levels in their bones.
options.B: Children experience lower impact forces during play.
options.C: Children's bones lack a periosteum protective layer.
options.D: Children's bones are softer and more flexible.

explanation: Kids' bones are still growing, so they tend to bend and splinter on one side like a fresh green twig rather than snapping completely. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h2)

question: In a neurovascular check for a injured limb, what does the letter 'P' stand for?
explanation: Think of the 5 Ps: Pain, Pallor, Pulselessness, Paresthesia, and Paralysis. They help us quickly spot nerve and blood flow issues! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h3)

question: A patient with a new leg cast says their toes feel very numb and tingly. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and report findings
options.B: Massage the toes gently to restore normal local blood circulation
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and encourage deep breathing
options.D: Administer a prescribed oral sleeping pill to calm the patient

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags for trapped nerves or poor blood flow. Checking thoroughly and reporting right away keeps the patient safe. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h3)

question: What is the main goal of fracture reduction?

options.A: To permanently increase the overall length of the injured limb
options.B: To dissolve any blood clots that formed around the injury site
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for any pain medication
options.D: To restore the broken bone fragments back into proper anatomical alignment

explanation: Reduction simply means putting the broken bone ends back in their correct place so they can heal straight and strong. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h4)

question: Why is careful pin-site care so important for a patient with an external fixator?

options.A: To encourage faster bone mineralization around the pin insertion sites
options.B: To prevent bacteria from traveling down the metal pins into the bone
options.C: To stop the external metal frame from rusting over time
options.D: To prevent the skin from sticking permanently to the metal frame

explanation: Since the pins go through the skin, they create a pathway for germs. Keeping them clean stops nasty deep bone infections like osteomyelitis! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h4)

question: When handling a wet plaster cast, why should nurses use the palms of their hands instead of their fingertips?

options.A: To stop the wet plaster material from sticking permanently to skin
options.B: To prevent indentations that can cause pressure sores on the skin
options.C: To prevent the nurse from getting skin irritation from chemicals
options.D: To make sure the heavy cast does not crack before it dries

explanation: Fingertips leave deep dents in wet plaster. Those little flat spots can press painfully against the skin and cause pressure ulcers later. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h5)

question: During a home visit, you notice the weights for a patient's skin traction are resting on the floor. What is your very first action?

options.A: Document that the patient is non-compliant with bedrest orders
options.B: Remove the traction setup entirely because it is no longer effective
options.C: Ensure the weights hang freely without touching the floor or bed
options.D: Add extra weight to make up for the time the weights spent resting

explanation: Traction weights must always hang free! If they touch the floor, the pulling force stops, and the bones won't stay aligned. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h5)

question: Where should a patient place their body weight when walking with crutches?
explanation: Always push through the hands, not the armpits! Putting weight in the armpits can damage important nerves and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h6)

question: What is the correct gap to keep between the top of the crutch and the patient's armpit?

options.D: No gap, it should touch firmly

explanation: A 2 to 3 finger-width gap keeps the crutch from pressing into the armpit nerves while the patient walks. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h6)

question: Which nutrient is especially helpful for building collagen and healing bones?
explanation: Vitamin C is a superstar for building collagen—the framework that new bone tissue needs to grow on! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h7)

question: Why is checking bowel movements extra important for patients taking opioid pain medications for a fracture?

options.A: Pain medications speed up digestion too much and cause diarrhea.
options.B: Opioids destroy beneficial bacteria living inside the large intestine.
options.C: Opioids frequently cause significant and uncomfortable constipation.
options.D: Pain medications prevent the body from absorbing dietary calcium.

explanation: Opioids slow down the gut big time. Anticipating and preventing constipation is a huge part of keeping patients comfortable during recovery. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h7)

question: What is a major sign of compartment syndrome that sets it apart from normal fracture pain?

options.A: Severe pain that is not relieved by prescribed opioid pain medication
options.B: Sharp pain that completely disappears after taking deep breaths
options.C: Mild aching pain that occurs only when the patient stands up
options.D: Gradual itching underneath the cast as the bone begins to heal

explanation: When strong pain meds don't touch the pain at all, think compartment syndrome! It means dangerous pressure is building up inside the muscle. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h8)

question: Which complication of long bone fractures (like the femur) involves breathing trouble and a spotty rash?
explanation: Fat droplets from inside the bone marrow can slip into the bloodstream after a long bone break, traveling to the lungs and brain. Watch out for breathing issues and a petechial rash! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T11#GNS324_U4_T11_h8)
